excerpts.heading: Where Thumper lives (static, PC)
excerpts.text:
## Where Thumper lives (static, PC)

- **Type 16 is Thumper.** Character loader `0x00445020` switches on each pool
  slot's type; case `0x10` pushes `"chars2\thumper"` (`0x004DDEF0`,
  referenced at `0x0044531F`). Case `0x1D` (29) is `chars3\molt`, so the
  Battle Arena "grasshopper" in [[PC original level Blender maps]] is Molt, not
  Thumper.
- **One native placement:** Council Chamber (engine 2, `LEVEL02/LEVEL.RAW`),
  type-35 slot 1, script 9, stored (141, −1857, 101). Its native floor below
  is 1693.5, so he starts 3,550 units above it
  (`original-levels/03-council-chamber/original-map.json`).
- **The RAW pair is the disc files.** Council Chamber's 0x101/0x102 packets
  whose second dword is 16 equal `CD/CHARS2/THUMPER.ANM` (34,304 B) and
  `THUMPER.ALL` (11,804 B) after their 8-byte heads, byte for byte. All 174
  model faces use texture page 21; page 21 is absent from Moonlit's RAW. A
  render of it shows grasshopper skin, eyes and claws.

excerpts.heading: Hardware arm 1 (classic selector, null sink, controllers disabled)
excerpts.text:
## Hardware arm 1 (classic selector, null sink, controllers disabled)

`make session-audit` clean before launch. Game PID 218674 under gamescope
218308; 6/6 hardware markers, no software markers.

- **Load:** `bugs.log` shows `LOAD : Loading file R:\PC\BUGS\cd\chars2\thumper.anm`
  then `.all`. Nothing else requested them; the type byte did.
- **Spawn:** slot 10 read type 16, health 50, flags 0x52, script PC
  `0x004C7EE8`. The enemy total read 11 (10 + Thumper).
- **Berry:** walking onto the purple berry right of the spawn set
  `0x0059D9A7` to 4. It survived three deaths and reset to 0 only on level
  re-entry (EXP-20260818-004's selector).
- **Wake and drop:** when Flik approached, Thumper fell from −6766 to about
  the ground (−3192), flags became 0x4053/0x5053/0x1053, PC `0x004C7F02`.
  He chased Flik, cornered him against the valley wall and killed him four
  times. Frames show the tall grasshopper with spiky legs and wings, textured,
  dimmed by Moonlit's night light, and a purple splash on hits.
- **Damage:** 28 health changes between samples: 27 of −3 and one −6 (two
  hits). Health 50 → 32 → 11, then 38 → 32 → 26 → 11 → 0 in the second visit.
  His health persisted across Flik's deaths; level re-entry reset him.
- **Death:** at 0 his slot read type 0, health 0, flags 0x18D1 (0x880 set),
  respawn 0, PC `0x004C7F6A`. The game ran 10 s more with no fault in
  `launch.log`, and he did not return.
- **Lives:** before the fight Flik was once back at the spawn with health
  refilled (cause not sampled; a spider was beside him). The first in-fight
  death then ended the game (back to the Flik's Journey select). In the second
  visit three deaths respawned him in-level. Not investigated.
- **Model records:** `0x005A9660` entries were used up to index 200 of 300;
  the overflow flag `0x005C5960` read 0.
- Closed through the packet; audit clean. Log moved to `arm1/bugs.log`.

excerpts.heading: Static audit of the dependencies (research subagent, disassembly)
excerpts.text:
## Static audit of the dependencies (research subagent, disassembly)

Confirmed from instructions or data unless marked:

- **Script 9** (`0x004C7EE8`..`0x004C7F08`): frame sequence, a blocking fall
  (op6, mode 4) that spawns dust type 1 on landing, op11 subroutine 4
  (`0x00431C90`: `[0x0059EF70] = 60`, read only by `0x00431CB0`), then a loop
  of random waits and random targets around home. Nothing reads the engine.
- **Handler `0x0041C100`** only plays looping sound row 0x1A (sample 31,
  `WASPBUZZ.WAV`, present in banks 1–18). No damage either way.
- **The boss fight is engine-2 code.** Per-frame dispatcher `0x00418780`
  (table `0x004187E8`, called at `0x004145BB` with `[0x00861C84]`) sends
  engine 2 to `0x00431CB0`; init dispatcher `0x00418690` sends it to
  `0x00431BF0`. `0x00431CB0` reads slot 1 (`0x0059B6AC`) and slots 2/3. It
  plays hit voices, makes slot 2 or 3 his thrown projectile, and below
  health 21 runs a camera cut, script 13 and `[0x0059A5B0] = 1` (level won).
  The HUD health bar (`0x00416890`, at `0x0041725A`) also draws only in
  engine 2. Engine 1's routines are `0x004317D0`/`0x00431730`.
- **Damage** is `0x00429790`: purple −3, gold −4, blue and green −2; red is
  deflected because flag 0x40 is set. Health is record +0x6E from source
  +0x10 (50). At ≤ 0 he takes the ordinary kill path and, with source
  +0x11 = 0, is not respawned.
- **Sprites:** engine 1 and engine 2 copy byte-identical 50-descriptor sprite
  tables (`0x004DA6B0`, `0x004DA7B8`), so no effect on his path is missing.
- **RAW pair (inferred, strong):** `0x00465030` has no 0x101/0x102 case and
  no instruction compares against those tags; the loader reads the disc
  files. The pair is kept for parity with Moonlit's other creature types.
- **Do not use slots 25 or 63:** engine 1's update writes through slot 25
  (Dot) unchecked, and level start special-cases slot 63.

excerpts.heading: Contradiction (recorded, not resolved)
excerpts.text:
## Contradiction (recorded, not resolved)

The static audit says homing selection `0x00428400` needs flags bit 0x0001,
which 0x0052 lacks, so green/purple homing "never" picks Thumper. At runtime
his flags were 0x4053/0x5053/0x1053 after waking, which have bit 0x0001.
Purple hits landed, but no arm instrumented whether a shot homed.
**Discriminating experiment:** with Thumper awake and no other enemy near,
sample the projectile's target pointer +0x10 and flag +0x33 bit 0x08 after a
purple throw.

*Later (2026-10-05):* [[EXP-20261005-002 - Native bosses and tough enemies in Moonlit Cliffs]]
saw bit 0x0001 appear on every boss once awake. Airborne bosses (1,974 and
2,304 up) took purple hits, and a frame shows a berry climbing toward the
flying Hopper. That supports lock-on; the projectile sample is still not taken.

excerpts.text:

- **Confirmed (static):** the boss behaviour, health bar and win are not in

  user's play.

excerpts.heading: Hardware arms
excerpts.text:
## Hardware arms

`arm.py NAME [ROUNDS] [SLOTS]` launches through EXP-001's `launch.sh`. Every
arm had 6/6 hardware markers and no software markers. It takes a purple
berry and walks through the gate. It then fights each slot with EXP-001's
`goto.py` (camera-relative keys, throws of 16, backing off within 900), and
closes through the packet with a clean `make session-audit`. Every run moved
its `bugs.log` into the packet. No game fault appears in any `launch.log`.
No memory was written.

| Creature | Behaviour in Moonlit | Damage | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| Molt | On the ground; wandered, then chased and killed Flik once | 14 × −3 | Killed, removed |
| Hopper (Canyon Showdown) | Dropped 346 to the ground; chased | 10 × −3 | Killed, removed |
| Hopper (Anthill Pt 2) | Flew at spawn height (1,974 up), drifting | −3 steps, 99 → 0 | Killed, removed |
| Hopper (Riverbed Flight) | Hovered fixed 2,468 up | none in 96 throws | Immune |
| Bird (Bird Nest) | Flew 2,304 up, drifting; never hurt Flik | −3 steps, 50 → 0 | Killed, removed |
| Bird (Cliffside) | Flew 2,035 up, drifting | none | Immune |
| Bird (Canyon Showdown) | Hovered fixed 1,786 up | none | Immune |
| Thud | Floated fixed 1,364 up | 50 → 0 twice | Killed, **respawned** at 50, killed again |
| Grasshopper | Dropped 1,471 to the ground and moved | yes | Killed |
| Roach | Moved toward Flik; Flik lost health during the fight | yes | Killed |
| Hspider | Moved about 800 from its spawn | yes | Killed |
| Taxi bug | Ran far east (to x ≈ 19,000) | yes | Killed |
| Fly | Dormant until Flik came near, then flew | yes | Killed (respawns natively) |
| Centipede | Stays at its spawn, pops up (`0x4045`) and retracts (`0x48C5`); killed Flik once | none in 4 rounds | Inconclusive (see below) |

- **Flags on waking.** Every boss gained bit `0x0001` once awake, usually
  with `0x4000` (for example 0x44 → 0x4045, 0x144 → 0x4145, 0x984 → 0x4985).
- **Homing reaches airborne targets.** The Anthill Pt 2 Hopper and the Bird
  Nest bird took −3 hits while 1,974 and 2,304 units up. A frame
  (`hopper-anthill-2/goto-fight0-throw3-…`) shows a purple berry climbing
  toward the flying Hopper. This is consistent with homing locking on, which
  EXP-001 recorded as contradictory. No projectile record was sampled.
- **Centipede.** The berries homed onto the respawned fly overhead instead.
  Frames show them climbing toward it while the centipede sits beside Flik.
  Its damage is untested, not refuted.
- **Bird height.** The user notes the bird is "up" by default, as in the
  original game, where a berry-shooter plant that fires straight up is
  needed. All three birds keep their native height (flag 0x04 holds target
  Y). In Moonlit only the homing berry reaches the vulnerable one.

excerpts.heading: Static audit (research subagent; confirmed unless marked)
excerpts.text:
## Static audit (research subagent; confirmed unless marked)

- **No crash path (inferred from confirmed parts).**
  - Reachable script code uses no op4, op10 or op11.
  - Sounds return early when a sample is not loaded (`0049D820`).
  - Kill and release take the default arm for types 22/29/30/36.
  - Sprite tables share entries 0–49 across engines 1, 6, 8, 9, 11, 13, 14
    and 15. The extra entries 50–52 feed only level-routine effects (rain,
    feathers, crowd).
- **Health ≥ 100 is immune** (`cmp ax,0x64` at `0x00429C35`). Flag 0x80 makes
  a creature unhittable, and 0x800 makes the contact routine ignore it
  (`0x0041CD7F`). Flag 0x04 is flying (holds target Y); 0x40 deflects red.
- **Respawn byte.** 101 is a literal 101-frame countdown, which is why Thud
  returns. 100 uses a per-type table delay. 0 removes the creature.
- **Scripts.** 11, 22 and 26 wander around home; 18 hovers (radius 0); 19
  and 29 idle. 28's tail runs only when engine 15 writes its program counter.
- **The fights are level routines**, from per-frame table `0x004187E8` and
  init table `0x004186FC`:
  - **Cliffside** `0x004345F0`: the bird tracks Flik and kills him when he
    falls into a band; an enforcer, not a fight.
  - **Riverbed Flight** `0x004361C0`: Hopper follows Flik's trail and taunts.
  - **Anthill Pt 2** `0x004369B0`/`0x00436B40`: Hopper flies a path, lowers
    per hit and releases Atta at health 90; the win comes from slot 23.
  - **Bird Nest** `0x00438040`: the bird chases high; below 21 the level
    is won.
  - **Battle Arena** `0x00439410`: hurt animation, crowd projectiles; win
    below 21.
  - **Bug Bar** `0x00439E90`: Thud shuttles, throws, and hits count only at
    the two ends; 8 counted hits win.
  - **Canyon Showdown** `0x0043AE00`: Hopper runs a waypoint table on hits;
    the bird carries him off with a movie.
- **Engine 1's routines touch only slot 25 and path 1** (`0x004317D0`,
  `0x00431730`).
- **Side effect.** Immune donors keep the enemies-left count
  (`0x0059D99E`) above 0, so an all-enemies trigger cannot fire.

excerpts.heading: "Visual artifacts when Flik starts moving"
excerpts.text:
## "Visual artifacts when Flik starts moving"

Three of nine post-move frames in the boss arms showed the view mostly
covered by dark horizontal bands. Camera pose and model did not explain it
(bird-nest and bird-cliffside share both). A **discriminating burst test**
captured about 10 frames per second through three cycles of right, up and
down starts:

- the boss-free control copy `EXP-20261005-002-control` (production
  reflinked);
- the Thud image.

The control showed the bands in 2 of 236 frames (`control-burst/burst-right3-00/01`),
while Flik turned beside the spawn with the camera near the east fence
(about (6870, 14830)). Thud's image showed them in 0 of 234. So the bands
**predate the transplants**: an intermittent camera view beside the spawn
fence. Their cause is not identified (camera near the fence or terrain is a
guess). If the user saw something different, it is still open.

excerpts.heading: Confirmed, inferred, unknown
excerpts.text:
## Confirmed, inferred, unknown

- **Confirmed (runtime):** all 14 load, render and run without a fault. The
  outcomes in the table. Thud respawns. Three bosses are immune.
- **Confirmed (static):** immunity at 100+, respawn semantics, the
  level-routine locations, identical shared sprite entries.
- **Inferred:** that homing locks on (airborne hits and the frame, no
  projectile sample); that the bands are a camera clip.
- **Unknown:** the centipede's damage; sound (null sink); behaviour over
  long play; the cause of the bands.

excerpts.heading: Change

## Change

`reimplementation/ablpc/anthill_scenery.py`:

- `NATIVE_SHELLS` gains loose leaf 14 → 127, hollow plant 209 → 87 and broad
  leaf 227 → 175. These are translated like the five existing pairings,
  with every payload and record byte other than XYZ kept.

  kind-0x101 strips 183/182/181/179. Only the points' X/Z move; the header,

The hollow plant's 656-byte auxiliary span is still unused for collision;

excerpts.heading: Native evidence (offline, original instructions)
excerpts.text:
## Native evidence (offline, original instructions)

`scripts/anthill-scenery-probe.py` (packet `native-candidate-03.json`, copied
to `reports/anthill-scenery/EXP-20261005-004-native.json`) accepts all 32 solid
props, 97 samples, with 1,632 relocation pointers exact. New this time:

- **Loose leaves (3) and broad leaves (2):** landings settle on their own
  shell.
- **Hollow plant:** two rim landings, and four lateral wall cases that push
  Flik 4,605–5,165 world units against the same shell lowered out of reach.
  The wall case was added for this prop.
- **Yellow leaves (8 × 4 sides):** grounded walks toward the stem. The loader
  links strips into `0x007F3D3C`. With the strip, Flik stops 113–142 stored
  units short of the centre (half-widths 103/130). Without it he walks 130–157
  past the centre.
- Every new case reproduces the original source at its original Anthill

excerpts.heading: Hardware evidence (matched arms)
excerpts.text:
## Hardware evidence (matched arms)

Each target has two images, both production with the start moved beside the
prop (12 bytes at VA `004DC7F4`). The candidate image also has the candidate
TERRAIN.ALL. `make_images.py` checks that nothing else differs. `walk.py` walks
straight toward a goal without jumping and logs Flik every step. All eight
arms passed the 6/6 hardware gate, logged no fault and closed with a clean
audit. A first launch was refused before any process started because the
image's `build.json` named the wrong EXE hash; it is kept as
`control-leaf-e-failed-launch`.

| Target | Control (production) | Candidate |
|---|---|---|
| Yellow leaf E, north from z 32300 | crosses the stem, reaches z 33572 in 4 steps | stops at z 32885–32889 (loop edge) for 39 holds |
| Hollow plant, south from z 32350 | passes 110 units from the cup centre, frame shows him inside | stops at the wall, never nearer than 384 units, frame shows him pressed against it |
| Grove loose leaf, north from z 33650 | stays at ground height (Y −5150) across the leaf | climbs onto it: Y −5261, then −5395 (245 above ground), frame shows him on top |
| Grove broad leaf, north from z 31900 | rises 45 units, stops at z ≈ 33120 under the blade | stops at z ≈ 32860 against the leaf's stalk |

The broad leaf was solid before too, but its edge moves. The original shell
stops Flik at the stalk lying in front of the blade, where the authored
approximation let him past it.

excerpts.heading: Diagnosis
excerpts.text:
## Diagnosis

- **Not authored geometry.** `analysis/proj.py` projects every room R scene
  mesh from the recorded camera (−5173, −3675, −10010; yaw about 1290; f 337,
  centre row 240). It matches the frame's wall top (row ≈215) and ramp, but
  rows 158–215 hold only sky and one reed (`analysis/r1.png`).
- **Not the panorama.** R's 128×96 backdrop has wavy blue, teal and green
  layers (`analysis/backdropR.png`), and the night sky hides it.
- **Non-physical motion.** Between two frames, a camera 158 units higher put
  the band higher on screen (rows 150 vs 158). No world object at any
  distance can do that.
- **Wrap.** EXP-20260916-011 showed that `0045A7F0` narrows camera-space
  coordinates to signed 16 bits. `analysis/wrap.py` applies that to R's eight
  terrain chunks from the same camera:
  - chunk 160 has 373 out-of-range vertices, chunk 490 has 326 (up to 40,336
    ahead) and chunk 489 has 70;
  - their faces fill a full-width, straight-topped band at rows 140–210
    (`analysis/wrapR.png`).
- **Guard absent in the rooms.** The EXP-20260916-011 guard matches by DAT
  offset and vertex count, for level 1 and only Moonlit's eight rows. In the
  user's process its counters (`.camdata` stats `0x010E1000`) were all zero.
  Room R's chunks (scenes 160 and 484–490, offsets 488,620–768,628) are not
  in the table.
- **Exposure.** Every room's terrain spans 52–57k units per axis and the hub
  58.6k along its corridor, past the ±32,767 range. Q is 3k across.

This dates from the rooms' first build (EXP-20260928-001), not the
2026-10-02 themes, which changed no geometry.

excerpts.heading: Fix
excerpts.text:
## Fix

`terrain_camera_guard.guard_table` builds one table from every DAT loaded as
level 1: Moonlit, the Journey hub and ROOMR–ROOMZ (8 + 8 + 72 = 88 rows). The
native code is unchanged, apart from its row count. The build refuses:

- an offset shared by two DATs, because the native search stops at the
  first offset match;
- any DAT holding another row's vertex count at that row's offset, which
  would let a foreign mesh borrow the row and its byte bound.

`dream_levels` keeps each chunk's `scene_index` in the room receipt, and
Studio passes the hub and rooms as extra sources.

excerpts.heading: Validation
excerpts.text:
## Validation

- **Tests:** `tests/test_terrain_camera_guard.py` has 24 passing, 2 of them new:
  - an emulated lookup filters a second row's mesh and never borrows a
    foreign row;
  - the private production union is unique, has an exact inverse and
    rejects collision and borrowing.

  The dream-level, grass, Studio, hub and chunk suites pass: 329 checks.
  The non-R2q suite had 7,268 passed and 19 failed. All 19 predate this
  change: they also fail on a clean HEAD checkout
  ([[Known Unknowns#Current regression-gate failure]]).
- **Build:** `work/copies/studio-1791047899927549753`, EXE
  `c3d8b207267b416679e963254dff837b7c8e6060136627e8c991c62120ad9027`, campaign
  `251578ca…` unchanged. All 765 CD files are byte-identical to

excerpts.heading: Observed
excerpts.text:
## Observed

- **Record grammar.** `+0x02` frames (`& 0x7FFF`), `+0x04` parts, `+0x06`
  words per frame, `+0x08` list count, `+0x0A` bitmask length, part list,
  bitmask, frames. With the bitmask length respected, **303 records in 60 of
  61 files end with zero slack**; every `+0x00` equals its slot.
  `LEVEL00/ROSIEWLK.ANM` is the exception (first offset beyond its file).
- **FLICK.ANM.** 40 slots, slot 26 absent; 24 parts (21 driven, 3 `-2`);
  frame counts 8–58; words per frame 129/126 (full body), 72 (parts 9–20) and
  57 (parts 0–8). Five slots are half-body layers.
- **State table.** 35 rows at `0x004C1CE8`, a `0xFFFFFFFF` word at
  `0x004C1FA4`, idle tables at `0x004C1FA8/B8/C8`. Every script frame lies
  within its slots. State `0x20` names absent slot 26 and no store writes
  `0x20`.
- **Coverage.** Sampler call sites: `0x004032FE`, `0x004033D9` (Flik),
  `0x00448569` (entity types), `0x0044CE05` (plants). Slots 7 and 12 have no
  reference. Berry-throw overlays use slots 2, 11 and 23; the strand swing
  uses slot 32 through header `+0x88`.
- **Variants.** FLICKD is identical; both FLICKP files have 29 parts and the
  same frame count in every present slot; CHARS4/FLICKP also lacks slots 30,
  31 and 37, exactly the fidgets its levels' idle table never picks.
- **Non-player models.** ATTAFLIK (actor slot 39, Riverbed Flight only) is
  drawn instead of Flik: `0x004362D0` copies his position and sets
  `0x0059D9A0` bit 0 (`0x0043634A`), which Flik's renderer tests at
  `0x0044C51A`; its slots are a flight loop, hurt, berry throw and death.
  FLIKHARV (actor slot 63, hook `0x00415E30`) is the rideable harvester:
  ridden moving, ridden standing, parked (`0x00416038`, `0x00416014`).
- **Triggers.** As tabulated in [[PC Flik animation catalog]] and
  `config/animation/pc-flik-animations.json`, each with addresses.

excerpts.heading: PC gold fragments
excerpts.text:
# PC gold fragments

A non-gold berry kill can drop the native spinning gold glyph as a
**fragment**. It pops up and falls exactly like the health leaf, then rests
where it lands. When Flik touches
it, the enemy counts on the gold-berry enemy counter and never respawns, as
after a gold-berry kill. Each berry has its own chance; gold already counts
and never drops one.
[[EXP-20261001-006 - Gold fragments from non-gold berry kills]] owns the
evidence; [[XPORT-20261001-013 - Gold fragment drop on non-gold kills]] owns
the PS1 comparison.

excerpts.heading: Setting
excerpts.text:
## Setting

Saved campaign key `gold_fragments` (Studio checkbox "Gold fragments"):

```json
"gold_fragments": {"enabled": true,
  "one_in": {"red": 12, "blue": 8, "green": 4, "purple": 2, "white": 12, "blackberry": 6},
  "seconds": 10}
```

- `one_in` is the chance per berry, from 1 (always) to 1000; 0 means never.
  All six keys are required.
- `seconds` (1–600) is how long a fragment lasts; it fades over its last
  16 frames.

These are the PS1 odds; the PS1 odds table has no white row, so white takes
red's (the PS1 project's white spread is a separate mod,
[[XPORT-20260909-011 - Custom white and black berry design]]). Save and build
to apply.

excerpts.heading: How it works
excerpts.text:
## How it works

- **Kill hook** `00429E00`: the berry-vs-enemy routine's call to `0041B9F0`.
  When the kill bits `[esp+0x10]` are 1 (not gold), it rolls the odds for
  `0059D9A7`. White and blackberry use the white-berry mode byte (`.wbstate`
  1/2) and are absent without that section. On a hit it spawns drop type
  0x78 as `0041B9F0` spawns the health leaf: at `(x, y − 0x1000, z)` with
  motion 0xD (vy −2048, gravity 128). It sets the leaf's floor and
  collectible flags and a 200-frame flight. The pool updater `0042B1F0`
  shadows the fall and lands it at `floor − 90×32`.
- **Retire hook** `0042B7D9`: the updater's retirement call. Where the leaf
  becomes the resting leaf (type 0x2A), a landed fragment stays in place:
  still, collectible, ground shadow (behaviour 2), its lifetime and an
  end-of-life fade. Any other ending is native. `+0x1C` is the updater's
  floor cache, so the actor is found from the helper's table, not a tag.
- **Pickup hook** `0042951E`: the pickup walker's default case. For the
  actor's latest fragment, while the actor is dying or dead, it does the
  gold block's bookkeeping: HUD pulse, `+0x62` = 0 (or the type cleared if
  already removed), the enemy count `0059D99E` down by one (not below 0) and
  the all-defeated call at zero. It plays the berry pickup sound.
- **Retirement:** every touched fragment keeps action 7 in `+0x2C`, the
  glyph's own and the berry pickups'. The walker default's 0xC would make
  `0042A2E0` call `00428AA0`, spawning type 0x40, whose sprite 0x33 is null
  in Moonlit Cliffs. That crashed the first hardware pickup (`004536D1`).
- **State** at the end of `.gfrag`: seed, kills, drops, credits, landed, 64 entries
  (each actor's latest fragment record) and 64 `cleared` bytes. The receipt
  gives the offsets.

excerpts.heading: Limits
excerpts.text:
## Limits

- Hardware so far: red-berry kills in Moonlit Cliffs (fixtures with every
  odds at 1). The fragment's fall was sampled frame by frame and matched the
  leaf's path; it landed at the game's floor − 90. Collected fragments
  counted (HUD 01/10, 02/10) and the enemies stayed gone. Other berries,
  levels, slopes, pits, water and the real odds have native tests only.
- Only berry kills drop fragments; contact kills (`0041C9B0`) do not.
- A fragment from an actor that has respawned gives no count and vanishes
  when touched.
- Fragments disappear when the camera is very far away (`0042B1F0` distance
  cull), like other drops.
- Scripted boss counts (`004369B0`, `0043AD00`, `00438720`) are untested.
  The fragment credit matches what a gold kill would do in `00429790`.
